name: bounded-particles-munk
title: Smoldyn particles bounded by center-based (viva-munk) discs: confinement, conservation across division, reaction equilibrium
claim: A Smoldyn particle sim composed with the munk backend keeps every cell's molecules strictly inside that cell's moving boundary (pymunk discs (oblong under crowding)), conserves molecule count when a cell divides (each molecule inherited by exactly one daughter, by containment), and lets the reversible reaction A+B<->C reach equilibrium inside the living tissue.
experiment: Run the `bounded_particles` composite with backend=munk on a small patch (~4 cells, seed_per_cell molecules of A and B) for ~18 steps with one scheduled division. Each step: advance the munk tissue (cells move/deform; one cell divides), then advance each cell's confined Smoldyn sim. Record per step, per cell: molecule positions + counts (A/B/C). Checks: (1) CONFINEMENT -- every molecule lies inside its cell's boundary each step; (2) CONSERVATION -- at the division step, the mother's count equals the sum over its two daughters; (3) REACTION -- A+B<->C relaxes toward the kf/kb equilibrium inside each cell.
outcomes: The flipbook overlay (reports/assets/bounded_particles_munk.html) -- particles coloured by cell, each inside its munk boundary, with a step/cell/molecule caption -- is the qualitative artifact; the confinement / conservation / reaction checks are the quantitative ones (pending run).
notes:
One of three parallel studies (cpm / vertex / munk) that run the SAME composite on the
three multicellular substrates, so the particle coupling can be compared across
paradigms. Smoldyn runs via SmoldynRunner (in-process on Linux 3.12, 3.11 subprocess
bridge on macOS).
